*.description: The product of the numbers; 1 for none.

+.description: The sum of the numbers; 0 for none.

-.description: z minus each w in turn; with one argument, its negation.

/.description: z divided by each w in turn; with one argument, its reciprocal. Exact division stays exact (1/3); a float divided by zero gives an infinity or NaN.

<.description: True if the numbers are strictly increasing.

<=.description: True if the numbers never decrease.

=.description: True if the numbers are all equal.

>.description: True if the numbers are strictly decreasing.

>=.description: True if the numbers never increase.

abs.description: The absolute value of the real number x.

acos.description: The arccosine of z; +nan.0 outside -1 to 1.

alist->hash-table.description: A new hash table of the pairs of alist; the first of a repeated key wins.

and.description: The first false value, or the last value; #t for none. Evaluation stops at the first false value.

append.description: A list of the elements of each list in turn, ending in x, which is shared, not copied.

apply.description: Calls proc with the elements of list as its arguments.

array->list.description: A list of the elements of a Smalltalk collection.

asin.description: The arcsine of z; +nan.0 outside -1 to 1.

assoc.description: The first pair of the association list whose car is equal? to key, or #f.

assq.description: The first pair of the association list whose car is eq? to key, or #f.

assv.description: The first pair of the association list whose car is eqv? to key, or #f.

atan.description: The arctangent of y, or of y/x in the right quadrant.

begin.description: Evaluates the forms in order and answers the last; at top level each is a top-level form.

bootstrap-compiler.description: Compiles the compiler source in directory with the running compiler, then with each new stage in turn, three times; answers the stages, for bootstrap-fixpoint? and bootstrap-differences. The last stage is left installed.

bootstrap-compiler-from-seed.description: As bootstrap-compiler, with a seed compiler (its entry points) as stage 0, as the image build does.

bootstrap-differences.description: The labels of the forms whose methods differ between stages i and j.

bootstrap-fixpoint?.description: True if stages 1, 2 and 3 of a bootstrap made the same methods: the compiler compiles itself into itself.

bootstrap-stage0.description: What stage 0 of a bootstrap was: the symbol seed.

call-with-input-file.description: Calls proc with an input port on the file, closed afterwards.

call-with-output-file.description: Calls proc with an output port on the file, closed afterwards.

call-with-values.description: Calls consumer with the values producer answers.

case.description: The body of the first clause with a datum eqv? to key; a clause may use => proc, called with key.

cdr.description: The second element of pair: for a list, the rest of it.

ceiling.description: The smallest integer not less than x; a float stays a float.

char->integer.description: The Unicode code point of char.

char-alphabetic?.description: True if char is a letter.

char-ci=?.description: True if the characters are the same, ignoring case.

char-lower-case?.description: True if char is a lower-case letter.

char-numeric?.description: True if char is a digit.

char-ready?.description: True: a character can always be read without waiting for it here.

char-upper-case?.description: True if char is an upper-case letter.

char-whitespace?.description: True if char is white space.

char<=?.description: True if the code points never decrease.

char<?.description: True if the code points are strictly increasing.

char=?.description: True if the characters are all the same.

char>=?.description: True if the code points never increase.

char>?.description: True if the code points are strictly decreasing.

char?.description: True if x is a character.

close-output-port.description: Closes the output port, so what was written is in its file.

command-line.description: A list of the program name and its arguments, as strings.

compile-form.description: The Smalltalk CompiledMethod that runs datum, made by the compiler in use. reader is the LISP reader that read datum, so its procedures keep their text.

complex?.description: True if x is a number: there are no non-real numbers built in.

compute-restarts.description: A list of the active restarts, innermost first.

cond.description: The body of the first clause whose test is true; with =>, proc called with the test value; else matches anything.

condition-report.description: The text that describes the condition c, as the runner shows it.

condition?.description: True if x is a condition: anything raised or signalled.

cons.description: A new pair whose car is a and whose cdr is b.

cos.description: The cosine of z, in radians.

current-input-port.description: The port read reads from by default.

current-load-path.description: The full path of the file being loaded or run, or #f.

current-output-port.description: The port display and write write to by default.

define.description: Defines name, globally at top level or locally at the start of a body. A body that starts with a string keeps it as its documentation.

define-macro.description: A macro that is not hygienic: its expander gets the operands and answers code, whose names mean what they mean where it is used.

define-number-syntax.description: A new number syntax for the reader and string->number: a token that no built-in syntax reads and that satisfies predicate is read as (parser token).

define-special-form.description: Makes name a special form of the running compiler: translator, called with the compiler's state, the form, the scope and whether the form is in tail position, answers its code. The documentation is what (documentation name) answers.

define-syntax.description: A hygienic macro, at top level or local to a body.

denominator.description: The denominator of the rational q in lowest terms, always positive.

digit-value.description: The value of the digit char, or #f if it is not a digit.

disassemble.description: Writes the bytecode of the procedure proc.

display.description: Writes x for a person: strings and characters as they are, to port or the current output.

do.description: A loop: binds each var to its init, then until test is true runs the body and steps each var; answers the results.

documentation.description: The documentation of what the symbol name means: a special form, a macro or a procedure; #f if it has none. Its first line is the call form.

documentation-category.description: The section of the reference of the built-ins that name belongs in, or #f.

dynamic-wind.description: Calls before, thunk and after, and calls after however thunk is left.

eof-object.description: The eof object, which reading answers at the end of its input.

eof-object?.description: True if x is the eof object.

eq?.description: True if a and b are the same object.

equal?.description: True if a and b are eqv?, or pairs, vectors or strings with equal? contents.

eqv?.description: True if a and b are the same object, or numbers of the same exactness and value, or the same character.

error.description: Signals an error with message, and the irritants for its report.

error-object-irritants.description: The irritants of the error e, as a list.

error-object-message.description: The message of the error e.

error-object?.description: True if x is an error, as error and the system signal them.

eval.description: Compiles and runs form at top level, and answers its value.

even?.description: True if the integer n is even.

exact.description: The exact number equal to z: a float gives the fraction it holds exactly. An error for an infinity or NaN.

exact-integer-sqrt.description: Two values: the largest integer s with s*s not above n, and n - s*s.

exact-integer?.description: True if x is an exact integer.

exact-rational?.description: True if x is an exact integer or an exact fraction.

exact?.description: True if the number z is exact.

exit.description: Ends the program: (exit) and (exit #t) succeed, (exit #f) fails, (exit n) exits with n.

exp.description: e raised to the power z.

expt.description: z1 raised to the power z2: exact for an exact base and an exact integer power.

file-error?.description: True if x is an error from opening a file.

file-exists?.description: True if there is a file at path.

find-restart.description: The innermost active restart named name, or #f.

finite?.description: True if the number z is neither infinite nor NaN.

floor.description: The largest integer not greater than x; a float stays a float.

floor-quotient.description: The quotient of n by d, rounded toward minus infinity.

floor-remainder.description: The remainder of n by d after floor-quotient; it has the sign of d.

floor/.description: Two values: the quotient of n by d rounded toward minus infinity, and the remainder, which has the sign of d.

for-each.description: Calls proc on each element of list, in order, for its effect.

gcd.description: The greatest common divisor of the integers, never negative; 0 for none.

gensym.description: A new uninterned symbol, unlike any other, for a name a macro makes up.

get-environment-variable.description: The value of the environment variable name, a string, or #f if it is not set.

get-output-string.description: The string of what has been written to the output string port.

getter-with-setter.description: A procedure that does what get does and whose setter is set, as SRFI 17 specifies: (set! ((getter-with-setter get set) x) v) calls (set x v). get itself is left as it is.

guard.description: Evaluates the body; if it raises, binds var to what was raised and tries the cond clauses, raising again if none matches.

hash-table->alist.description: An association list of the keys and values of table.

hash-table-contains?.description: True if table has a value for key.

hash-table-copy.description: A new hash table with the keys and values of table.

hash-table-count.description: The number of keys in table.

hash-table-delete!.description: Removes key and its value from table.

hash-table-keys.description: A list of the keys of table, in the order they were added.

hash-table-ref.description: The value of key in table; if there is none, the result of calling missing, or an error.

hash-table-ref/default.description: The value of key in table, or default.

hash-table-set!.description: Associates key with value in table.

hash-table-update!.description: Replaces the value of key with the result of calling proc on it.

hash-table-update!/default.description: As hash-table-update!, with default as the value of a missing key.

hash-table-values.description: A list of the values of table, in the order of their keys.

hash-table-walk.description: Calls proc on each key and its value.

hash-table?.description: True if x is a hash table.

if.description: Evaluates then if test is true (anything but #f), else else.

image-build-info.description: How this image was built: an association list of its seed, the bootstrap and its fixpoint.

inexact?.description: True if the number z is inexact (a float).

infinite?.description: True if the number z is +inf.0 or -inf.0.

integer->char.description: The character with the Unicode code point n.

integer?.description: True if x is an integer, exact or not: (integer? 2.0) is true.

invoke-restart.description: Transfers to the active restart (or the one with that name), with the arguments.

lambda.description: A procedure. params is (a b), (a b . rest) or rest; a body may start with internal definitions, and with a documentation string.

lcm.description: The least common multiple of the integers, never negative; 1 for none.

length.description: The number of elements of list; an error for an improper or circular list.

let.description: Binds each name to its init, evaluated outside the bindings; the named form also binds loop to the body as a procedure.

let*.description: As let, but each init sees the bindings before it.

let*-values.description: As let-values, but each expr sees the bindings before it.

let-syntax.description: Local macros, defined in the enclosing scope, for the body.

let-values.description: Binds the values of each expr to its formals, as lambda parameters, evaluated outside the bindings.

letrec.description: As letrec*: bindings visible to every init and the body.

letrec*.description: Bindings visible to every init and the body, assigned in order: for procedures that call each other.

letrec-syntax.description: Local macros that can use each other, for the body.

lisp-eval.description: Compiles and runs datum with the compiler in use, as eval does.

lisp-eval-string.description: Reads and evaluates every datum of string in turn, so procedures keep their text; answers the last value.

lisp-symbol.description: The LISP symbol spelled as x, a Smalltalk symbol or string.

list.description: A new list of the arguments.

list->array.description: A Smalltalk Array of the elements of list.

list->string.description: A new string of the characters of list.

list->vector.description: A new vector of the elements of list.

list?.description: True if x is a proper list: finite, and ending in the empty list.

load.description: Reads and evaluates every form of the file at path, relative to the file being loaded, and answers the full path of that file.

log.description: The natural logarithm of z, or its logarithm in base; -inf.0 at zero, +nan.0 below it.

macroexpand.description: form expanded until it is no longer a macro call.

macroexpand-1.description: form expanded once, if it is a macro call; else form itself.

magnitude.description: The magnitude of x: for a real number, its absolute value.

make-hash-table.description: A new hash table comparing keys with equality: eq?, eqv? or equal? (the default).

make-reader.description: A reader over string: reader-next reads its datums one at a time.

make-string.description: A new string of k characters, each char (a space by default).

make-vector.description: A new vector of k elements, each fill.

map.description: A new list of the results of calling proc on each element of list.

max.description: The largest of the real numbers; inexact if any of them is.

member.description: The first tail of list whose car is equal? to x, or #f.

memq.description: The first tail of list whose car is eq? to x, or #f.

memv.description: The first tail of list whose car is eqv? to x, or #f.

method-listing.description: A fingerprint of a CompiledMethod: its header, its bytecode bytes and its literals, blocks included, to compare two compilations.

min.description: The smallest of the real numbers; inexact if any of them is.

nan?.description: True if the number z is a NaN.

negative?.description: True if the real number x is less than zero.

not.description: True if x is #f, the only false value.

null?.description: True if x is the empty list.

number->string.description: The text of the number z, as write writes it, in radix.

number?.description: True if x is a number.

numerator.description: The numerator of the rational q in lowest terms.

odd?.description: True if the integer n is odd.

opal-run.description: Runs a CompiledMethod that compile-form made, and answers its value.

open-input-file.description: An input port reading the file at path.

open-input-string.description: An input port that reads the characters of string.

open-output-file.description: An output port writing the file at path, which is replaced.

open-output-string.description: An output port that collects what is written to it.

or.description: The first true value, or #f; evaluation stops there.

pair?.description: True if x is a pair.

peek-char.description: The next character from port, without reading it, or the eof object.

positive?.description: True if the real number x is greater than zero.

procedure->block.description: A Smalltalk block that calls proc, for Smalltalk code that wants one.

procedure-documentation.description: The documentation of proc, or #f: the call form on its first line, then what it does.

procedure-source.description: The text proc was compiled from, or #f for a primitive.

procedure?.description: True if x is a procedure.

quasiquote.description: The template as data, with (unquote x) and (unquote-splicing x), written ,x and ,@x, filled in.

raise.description: Raises obj to the current handlers; a handler that returns is an error.

raise-continuable.description: Raises obj; the value the handler returns is the value of raise-continuable.

rational?.description: True if x is a rational number: an exact rational, or a finite float.

rationalize.description: The simplest rational number within y of x; inexact if either is.

read.description: The next datum from port (the current input by default), or the eof object.

read-all.description: A list of every datum of string.

read-char.description: The next character from port, or the eof object.

read-error?.description: True if x is an error from reading.

read-framed-message.description: The next message on standard input, framed as the Language Server Protocol frames it (a Content-Length header, a blank line, the text), or the eof object.

read-from-string.description: The one datum string holds; an error for none or more than one.

read-line.description: The rest of the line from port, without its line break, or the eof object.

read-string.description: A string of the next k characters from port, fewer at its end, or the eof object.

reader-datum-start.description: The offset, from 0, at which the datum read last starts.

reader-next.description: The next datum, or the eof object at the end of the text.

reader-position.description: The offset, from 0, just after what the reader has read.

reader-range-of.description: The start and end offsets of the text the reader read the list from, or #f.

reader-source-for.description: The text the reader read the list from, or #f.

real?.description: True if x is a real number.

require.description: Loads the library name.lisp from the first folder of (hash-table-ref *env* 'library-path) that has it, once, and answers its full path; a name with slashes names a subfolder. The library path is the folders of COGLISP_PATH, then cog-lisp's own lib folder: (require 'cl) loads the Common Lisp names, (require 'test) the test library.

require-path.description: The full path of the file (require 'name) would load: name.lisp in the first folder of (hash-table-ref *env* 'library-path) that has it, or #f. Loads nothing.

restart-case.description: Evaluates form with named restarts; invoking one leaves form and evaluates its body with the arguments.

restart-name.description: The name of restart, a symbol.

reverse.description: A new list of the elements of list in reverse order.

round.description: The nearest integer to x, a half going to the even one; a float stays a float.

save-image.description: Saves the running image, so its definitions are there when it next starts.

send.description: Sends a Smalltalk message; the selector is spelled as in Smalltalk (at:put:).

set!.description: Assigns value to the variable name, local or global. With a call as its target it assigns through the setter of proc, as SRFI 17 specifies: ((setter proc) arg ... value), so (set! (car x) v) sets the first element of x and (set! (vector-ref v i) x) a slot of v.

set-car!.description: Replaces the car of pair with x.

set-cdr!.description: Replaces the cdr of pair with x.

setter.description: The procedure (set! (proc arg ...) value) calls, as (s arg ... value): set-car! for car, set-cdr! for cdr, vector-set! for vector-ref, string-set! for string-ref, hash-table-set! for hash-table-ref and for hash-table-ref/default, and any a program adds with (set! (setter proc) s). Signals an error if proc has none. The setters of the built-in getters cannot be changed.

sin.description: The sine of z, in radians.

smalltalk.description: The Smalltalk global Name, such as a class.

smalltalk-global.description: The Smalltalk global named name (a symbol or a string), or #f.

smalltalk-nil.description: Smalltalk nil, which is not a LISP value.

smalltalk-nil?.description: True if x is Smalltalk nil.

smalltalk-object?.description: True if x is a Smalltalk object that is not also a LISP value.

smalltalk-send.description: Sends the message selector to receiver with the arguments, chosen at run time.

special-form-names.description: The names of the special forms, sorted.

sqrt.description: The square root of x: exact for an exact perfect square, else inexact. An error for a negative number (complex numbers are not built in).

stack-depth.description: The number of frames on the stack, for testing that loops run in constant space.

store-value.description: Invokes the store-value restart with x.

string.description: A new string of the characters.

string->list.description: A list of the characters of string.

string->number.description: The number string reads as, or #f; radix is 2, 8, 10 or 16.

string-append.description: A new string of the characters of each string in turn.

string-ci=?.description: True if the strings are the same, ignoring case.

string-copy.description: A new string of the characters of string from start to end.

string-copy!.description: Copies the characters of from, start to end, into to at index at.

string-downcase.description: A new string of string in lower case.

string-fill!.description: Replaces every character of string with char.

string-index.description: The index of the first char in string, or #f.

string-join.description: A new string of the strings of list, with separator between them.

string-length.description: The number of characters of string.

string-ref.description: The character of string at index k, from 0.

string-search.description: The index where pattern first occurs in string, or #f.

string-set!.description: Replaces the character of string at index k with char.

string-split.description: A list of the parts of string between the occurrences of char.

string-trim.description: A new string of string without the white space at either end.

string-upcase.description: A new string of string in upper case.

string<=?.description: True if the strings never decrease, by code point.

string<?.description: True if the strings are strictly increasing, by code point.

string=?.description: True if the strings are all the same.

string>=?.description: True if the strings never increase, by code point.

string>?.description: True if the strings are strictly decreasing, by code point.

string?.description: True if x is a string.

substring.description: A new string of the characters of string from start to end.

subvector.description: A new vector of the elements of vector from start to end.

symbol->string.description: A new string of the name of symbol.

symbol?.description: True if x is a symbol.

syntax-error.description: Stops compilation with message and the forms, for a macro to report a misuse.

syntax-rules.description: The transformer of a hygienic macro: the first pattern a use matches gives its template, filled in.

tan.description: The tangent of z, in radians.

truncate.description: x with its fraction dropped, toward zero; a float stays a float.

truncate-quotient.description: The quotient of n by d, rounded toward zero.

truncate-remainder.description: The remainder of n by d after truncate-quotient; it has the sign of n.

truncate/.description: Two values: the quotient of n by d rounded toward zero, and the remainder, which has the sign of n.

unless.description: Evaluates the body when test is false.

use-value.description: Invokes the use-value restart with x.

values.description: Answers its arguments as several values; one value is just itself.

vector.description: A new vector of the arguments.

vector->list.description: A list of the elements of vector.

vector-append.description: A new vector of the elements of each vector in turn.

vector-copy.description: A new vector of the elements of vector from start to end.

vector-fill!.description: Replaces every element of vector with x.

vector-for-each.description: Calls proc on each element of vector, in order.

vector-length.description: The number of elements of vector.

vector-map.description: A new vector of the results of calling proc on each element of vector.

vector-ref.description: The element of vector at index k, from 0.

vector-set!.description: Replaces the element of vector at index k with x.

vector?.description: True if x is a vector.

when.description: Evaluates the body when test is true.

with-exception-handler.description: Calls thunk with handler handling what it raises.

with-input-from-file.description: Calls thunk with the current input read from the file.

with-output-to-file.description: Calls thunk with the current output written to the file.

with-output-to-string.description: Calls thunk with its output collected, and answers it as a string.

write.description: Writes x so that read reads it back: strings in quotes, characters as #\x.

write-framed-message.description: Writes text to standard output, framed as the Language Server Protocol frames it.

write-shared.description: Writes x with a datum label for every part it shares, so the sharing reads back.

write-string.description: Writes the characters of string to port.

zero?.description: True if z is zero, exact or inexact.
